title: Contingency Coordinator Handbook and Rotation Patterns
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This document defines the Contingency Coordinator role, a standardized rotation pattern, and a compact operational handbook for first-hour decision-making during service-impacting events. It combines a lightweight decision canvas with concrete runbook fragments, customer communication templates, and a repeatable game-day design for onboarding responders. The goal is to reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) and improve customer comms consistency while preserving responder ergonomics.

Scope:
- Applies to all incidents that impact customer-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated pools, control plane).
- Low-noise operational issues (single-tenant infra jobs, non-customer-facing infra) may use local team runbooks; coordinate with SRE if escalation is possible.

Key definitions:
- Contingency Coordinator (CC): 1-person role responsible for orchestration, cross-team comms, and status updates for the first 60–120 minutes.
- Primary Responder: owns remediation actions (service fixes, config changes).
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge (Zoom/Slack) and captures timeline.

Service SLOs and thresholds to trigger CC:
- Availability: hosted inference API: 99.9% monthly. Trigger: sustained <99.0% for 10 minutes or customer-impacting errors >0.5% of requests in 5 minutes.
- Latency: 95th token latency <200 ms for plain text generation endpoints. Trigger: 95th increased by 2x sustained for 10 minutes.
- Error budget: if monthly error budget consumption >30% before the 15th of the month, set CC for degradations that normally would be routed to escalation.

Roles and responsibilities (quick reference):
- Contingency Coordinator:
  - Triage and declare incident severity using Decision Canvas (see below).
  - Open bridge, assign Primary/Secondary, and document scope.
  - Author initial status update within 15 minutes.
  - Coordinate customer notices with Customer Success Liaison for impacted customers.

- Primary Responder:
  - Execute remediation steps from the runbook, escalate to SRE Lead when blocked.
  - Record actions and timestamps in the bridge notes.

- Bridge Operator:
  - Maintain the running timeline and collect artifacts (logs, traces, dumps).
  - Close bridge when verification criteria met.

Decision Canvas (one-page):
- Use this checklist in the first 5–10 minutes to set severity and next steps:
  1) Detection source: alert / customer report / monitoring anomaly?
  2) Blast radius: single customer / subset / global?
  3) Impact type: correctness / latency / availability / data loss?
  4) Workaround available? (yes => consider downgrade/route around)
  5) Customer exposure: large customers on dedicated pools?
  6) Automated rollback available? (yes/no)
  7) Suggested severity: Sev2 (degraded but usable) | Sev1 (major outage) | Sev3 (minor, ticketable)

First-hour runbook (step-by-step):
1) Triage & confirm (0–10m)
   - CC acknowledges alert, annotates in pager system, and opens bridge.
   - Record detection ID, alert query, and recent deploys.
2) Fast containment (10–30m)
   - If a traffic-routing workaround is possible: execute "route-avoid" to healthy region; document command and regen keys.
   - If KV cache pressure is suspected: increase kv-cache eviction threshold to 0.6 and monitor miss-rate.
3) Remediation loop (30–90m)
   - Primary runs targeted remediation play: roll back recent control-plane deploy -> follow deploy-rollback checklist.
   - If hardware/instance failure: promote standby nodes in dedicated pool using the infra-swap script.
4) Verification & close (90–120m)
   - Run synthetic test suite (api/synthetic/generate-quick-check) until passing for 15 minutes.
   - CC drafts final status, Bridge Operator closes bridge, Primary creates post-incident ticket with artefacts.

Runbook fragments (copyable commands and checks):
- Check API health: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s' https://api.redwood.ai/health
- Promote standby node: infractl pool promote --pool dedicated-pool-1 --node standby-42
- Increase kv-cache eviction: redis-cli -h kvcache-01 CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru

Escalation matrix (ordered):
1) Primary Responder -> Team Lead (service owning team)
2) SRE Lead -> Platform Engineering Manager
3) CTO operations pager (only Sev1 after 60m unresolved or cascading failures)

Customer communications (templates)
- Initial holding notice (first 15m):
  Subject: Incident affecting Redwood inference API — we’re investigating
  Body: Hi {CustomerName},
  We detected an issue affecting inference requests to the API starting at {start_time} UTC. Some requests may return errors or experience increased latency. Our engineering team has opened an incident and is actively investigating. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.
  - Impact: {brief impact summary}
  - Affected endpoints: {endpoints}
  - Temporary workaround: {workaround if any}
  Thank you for your patience.

- Escalated update (30–60m if no resolution):
  Subject: Update on incident affecting inference API — targeted mitigation in progress
  Body: Hi {CustomerName},
  We continue to investigate. We have implemented a targeted mitigation ("{mitigation_action}") to reduce customer impact. We are monitoring health metrics and will follow up again within 60 minutes with next steps or ETA for full restoration.

- Resolution notice (close):
  Subject: Incident resolved — inference API (root cause & remediation)
  Body: Hi {CustomerName},
  The issue that began at {start_time} has been resolved as of {resolved_time} UTC. Root cause: {root_cause_summary}. Actions taken: {actions}. Impacted customers: {list if small}. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a formal post-incident report within 3 business days.

Status page update payload (example JSON):
{
  "status": "investigating",
  "components": [{"id": "inference-api", "status": "degraded_performance"}],
  "impact": "partial",
  "notice": "We are investigating elevated error rates and latency for the inference API.",
  "updated_at": "{iso_timestamp}"
}

Rotation pattern and scheduling norms:
- Standard CC rotation cadence: 1 week on-call for Contingency Coordinator, overlapping with primary oncall shifts to ensure knowledge transfer.
- Shadow week: the incoming CC shadows outgoing CC for 2 business days before handover.
- Max contiguous weeks: 2. After 2 weeks, require 7-day rest period.
- Swap policy: CC swaps allowed with 48-hour notice and approval by rotation owner.

Handoff checklist (for rotation changeover):
- Prepare a 10-minute briefing covering: recent incidents, ongoing mitigations, outstanding postmortems, and current SLO consumption.
- Export current bridge notes and unresolved tickets into the rotation folder (s3://redwood-ops/cc-rotation/{week}).
- Confirm calendar blocks for the upcoming week’s game-day & runbook drills.

Game-day design (90–120m exercise):
- Learning goals: practice CC decision canvas, customer notice cadence, and cross-team orchestration.
- Scenario template: KV-cache eviction storm causing increased latency for multi-tenant hosted API.
- Success criteria: initial customer holding notice within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 30 minutes, and restoration by 90 minutes in at least 80% of runs.
- Post-exercise: complete a micro-retro using this template: what went well / what blocked us / action items (owner + due date).

Post-incident report skeleton (deliver within 3 business days):
- Title and incident timeline (ordered timestamps)
- Summary and customer impact
- Root cause analysis (technical and systemic)
- Action items (owner, due date, verification plan)
- Metrics: MTTA, MTTR, error budget impact, customer-facing incidents count
- Learnings and follow-ups (policy, tooling, runbook updates)

Metrics for continuous improvement:
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) goal: <5 minutes during business hours.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) goal: <60 minutes for Sev2, <180 minutes for Sev1 (containing full restoration path).
- Postmortem closure rate: 95% of incidents that hit CC must have postmortem started within 3 business days.

Automations and tools referenced:
- Pager service: ops-pager.redwood.ai (alerts and on-call annotations)
- Bridge template: /templates/bridge/contingency-bridge.md (link internal)
- Synthetic checks: monitors/api/synthetic/generate-quick-check (CI job)

Appendix: quick examples and snippets
- Bridge opening command: bridgectl open --title "Contingency: {service}" --severity Sev2 --owners team-ml@redwood.ai
- Slack status snippet (short): :warning: Incident: inference-api — decreased performance. Initial mitigation: routing to eu-region. Update in 30m.

Ownership and governance:
- The CC rotation owner is the SRE team lead; rotation schedule lives in the SRE calendar and is managed by the Ops PM.
- Runbook maintenance: each team owning a service must update runbooks quarterly or after any bridge activation.

Related references:
- Incident runloop and comm stencils (internal)
- Bridge operator cheatsheet (internal)

Contact and feedback:
If you have feedback on this handbook, file a doc suggestion in the SRE team backlog or email oncall-feedback@redwood.ai.
